description:
The Distribution of Gypsum-Oil Seeds scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

This initiative aims to enhance agricultural productivity and promote sustainable farming practices. 

The scheme is particularly focused on improving soil health and increasing the yield of oilseed crops. 

The Indian government recognized the need for this scheme due to the rising demand for edible oils in the country. 

India is one of the largest consumers of edible oils globally, with a consumption of approximately 23 million metric tons in 2020. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to distribute gypsum and oil seeds to farmers at subsidized rates. 

The government aims to cover around 1 million farmers under this scheme in its initial phase. 

The targeted beneficiaries include small and marginal farmers who are often unable to afford quality seeds and soil amendments. 

The scheme also aims to increase the area under oilseed cultivation by 20 percent over the next five years. 

Farmers participating in the scheme can receive up to 50 kilograms of gypsum per hectare. 

The subsidy provided for gypsum is approximately 50 percent of the market price. 

The market price of gypsum is around INR 300 per 50 kilograms. 

Thus, the subsidy translates to about INR 150 per 50 kilograms for the farmers. 

In addition to gypsum, the scheme provides various oilseed varieties such as mustard, soybean, and groundnut. 

Farmers can receive up to 5 kilograms of oilseed seeds per hectare under the scheme. 

The subsidy on oilseed seeds is also set at 50 percent of the market price. 

The market price for oilseed seeds varies but is approximately INR 200 per kilogram for mustard seeds. 

Therefore, the subsidy for oilseed seeds can amount to around INR 100 per kilogram. 

The total financial assistance a farmer can receive under this scheme can reach up to INR 1,500 per hectare. 

This assistance is aimed at reducing the financial burden on farmers and encouraging them to adopt better agricultural practices. 

To be eligible for the scheme, farmers must be registered under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme. 

This registration ensures that the farmers are recognized and can access various government benefits. 

Farmers must also possess a valid landholding certificate to prove their ownership of agricultural land. 

The age limit for eligibility is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme. 

The application process for the Distribution of Gypsum-Oil Seeds scheme is straightforward. 

Farmers need to visit the nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or Agricultural Department office. 

They must fill out an application form provided by the authorities. 

Required documents include a copy of the landholding certificate and proof of registration under PM-KISAN. 

Farmers must also submit an identity proof such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the concerned authorities. 

Upon successful verification, farmers will receive the gypsum and oilseed seeds at subsidized rates. 

The distribution of gypsum and oil seeds is conducted during the Kharif and Rabi seasons. 

The Kharif season typically runs from June to September. 

The Rabi season usually spans from October to March. 

The government aims to complete the distribution process within two months of the application submission. 

This ensures that farmers can utilize the inputs in a timely manner for optimal crop yield. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

State Agricultural Departments are also involved in the execution and monitoring of the scheme. 

Farmers can contact the Ministry of Agriculture through their official helpline number 1800 180 1551 for any queries. 

Additionally, local agricultural officers are available for assistance at the district level. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to achieve self-sufficiency in edible oil production. 

India currently imports around 60 percent of its edible oil requirements. 

By promoting oilseed cultivation, the government aims to reduce dependency on imports. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the doubling of farmers' income by 2022 as per the government's vision. 

In terms of statistics, the area under oilseed cultivation in India was approximately 26 million hectares in 2020. 

The government aims to increase this area to 31 million hectares by 2025 through various initiatives including this scheme. 

The expected increase in oilseed production is projected to be around 2 million metric tons annually. 

This would significantly contribute to the overall agricultural GDP of the country. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable agricultural practices. 

Gypsum is known to improve soil structure and enhance water retention. 

This is particularly beneficial in regions facing water scarcity. 

The use of gypsum can also help in reducing soil salinity, improving crop health. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the initial phase of the scheme. 

This budget is aimed at ensuring the availability of quality inputs to farmers across the country. 

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in rural areas through increased agricultural activities. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt integrated farming practices for better results. 

The government also plans to conduct training programs for farmers on the effective use of gypsum and oil seeds. 

These training sessions will be organized by KVKs and local agricultural universities. 

The overall impact of the scheme is expected to be significant in terms of enhancing food security. 

By increasing domestic oilseed production, the scheme aims to stabilize prices in the market. 

This will ultimately benefit consumers as well as farmers. 

The Distribution of Gypsum-Oil Seeds scheme is a vital step towards achieving agricultural sustainability in India. 

It aligns with the government’s vision of promoting Atmanirbhar Bharat or self-reliant India. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to improve their livelihoods and contribute to national food security.
